description.description: one-line summary of what the benchmark is

why_people_use_it.description: why this benchmark matters / what decision it informs

metric.description: the scoring metric, e.g. accuracy, pass@1, F1, ELO

saturation.description: how close top models are to the ceiling

openness.description: how much of the benchmark the public can inspect: open (tasks or data and the method are public), partly-open (the method and some items are public, but the scored test set is private or held out), closed (the maker publishes only results and a description)

openness_note.description: one sentence, from the maker's own page, paper or repository: what is public and what is not

worked_examples.description: 3-5 category-appropriate worked examples, shown as a navigable carousel. Each is one success-vs-plausible-failure contrast; the UI derives panel labels + footer from `category` + `metric`. Author DISTINCT examples (different sub-tasks, difficulties, or failure modes), not variations of one.

task_type.description: subject/task label, e.g. 'College Physics' or 'Array manipulation'

input.description: the question STEM / task prompt WITHOUT the answer options (options go in `options`)

options.description: answer choices for a multiple-choice item, in order; the UI renders them lettered (A, B, C, ...). Omit for non-MCQ tasks (code, translation, agents, ...).

answer.description: the correct / passing / safe / truthful response. For MCQ, start with the letter, e.g. 'B — a rat pressing a lever'.
a PLAUSIBLE wrong/weak/unsafe/misleading response (never an obviously foolish one)

why.description: the exact reason it fails / loses points under this benchmark's scoring

checks.description: one sentence: the capability this contrast demonstrates

scoring.description: how the benchmark scores this item, e.g. 'exact-match accuracy', 'pass@1 over hidden tests', 'LLM-judge rubric', 'chrF/MetricX'
